content:
lina: Heads-up — several dashboards showed spike in main-thread CPU and slow interactive map layers after today's canary. p95 up ~2x for map-heavy dashboards. filing here to coordinate.

derek: thanks. is this the new map-tiles change from the split-chunk PR?

lina: potentially. can reproduce locally by loading dashboard with multiple map layers. profiler shows big parse/compile time right after bundle eval.

priya: any new polyfills pulled in? We had a late change that added a small fetch polyfill for older browsers in the chunk split.

lina: yes — analyzer shows added polyfill-core-js (~95kb gz) in vendor.map-chunk. bundle before: vendor.map-chunk.js.gz 410kb, after: 505kb.

tom: hmm polyfill is surprising — it should be lazy. which import triggered it?

lina: stacktrace points at map-utils -> detectPassiveEvents -> uses global feature detect that imported core-js. It looks like map-utils was moved from dynamic import to inline during the optimization PR to reduce flicker.

derek: moving from dynamic -> inline will pull transitive deps into the main bundle. That explains parse spike.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: Canary deploy completed for tag map-split-optim (4 instances) at 2026-03-18T18:02:10Z.

priya: two-pronged problem: (1) client parse/compile overhead from polyfill inclusion, (2) routing pressure — on canary some requests hit fallback route and backend telemetry shows spike in api-proxy latency. Could be quota misrouting because canary tag wasn't excluded from rate limits.

lina: I inspected client traces: long tasks during initial mount ~350-600ms across clients. network is fine. main thread blocked on bundle eval and then map-utils init.

tom: plan: hotfix the client to restore dynamic import for map-utils so polyfill stays lazy. Can we do that safely?

derek: yes. quick revert to dynamic import should restore tree-shaking. Also remove direct feature-detect import and replace with runtime check that only imports polyfill when needed:

```js
// before
import 'core-js/stable';
import { initMap } from './map-utils';

// after
async function ensurePolyfills(){
  if(!('passive' in SomeDetect)){
    await import('core-js/stable');
  }
}
const mapModule = await import('./map-utils');
mapModule.initMap();
```

priya: good. for the routing/quota part: the canary was leaked into production routing group A due to missing rollout-tag exclusion in policy. That caused per-route quotas to be evaluated incorrectly and some traffic fell back to region-b. Our routing policy config expects canaries to be tagged and excluded from aggressive throttles. I created PR to fix the policy.

lina: while the hotfix PR lands, can we temporarily promote sampling for canary telemetry to 100% and pause rollout to remaining hosts? we need better traces.

infra-bot: infra-bot: temporary telemetry sampling override applied for rollout-tag=map-split-optim -> sampling=100% (ID: t-over-881). Pause rollout: instance count locked to 1/4.

deploy-bot: rolling back canary instances to 1/4 per request from eng-platform.

derek: running local bundle analyzer after the revert patch shows vendor.map-chunk back to ~420kb gz. promising.

(10m later)

lina: quick smoke after hotfix: local p95 returned to baseline, long tasks gone. pushing canary host update now.

(25m later)

priya: canary host updated, traces show no long tasks, backend routing latency normalized after policy change. sampling capture helped correlate client traces with API proxy spikes.

lina: closing loop: action items - add a CI bundle-diff check that fails if a canary increases any chunk >50kb gz (sara-style guard) - add lint rule / code-review checklist: avoid inlining large dynamic modules that have side-effectful imports - update routing policy tests to ensure rollout-tag exclusion is present - auto-bump telemetry sampling to 100% for canaries (infra ticket created)

derek: I'll open the bundle-diff CI PR.

priya: I'll follow up on routing policy tests and the infra ticket.

lina: thanks all. small postmortem incoming. :handshake:
